---
title: "A user-supplied grammar"
format: html
---

Java properties files are not one of Quarto's built-in highlighting
languages. This project adds them by shipping a tree-sitter grammar in
`_quarto/grammars/properties/`: the compiled `properties.wasm` and its
`highlights.scm` query. Any code block marked `properties` now picks it
up:

```properties
# Application settings
server.port = 8080
server.address = localhost
app.name = Report Builder
app.data-dir = ${HOME}/reports
```

Inline code works the same way: `retries = 3`{.properties}.

The grammar's capture names become CSS classes: a capture `@name.sub`
is emitted as `<span class="hl-name-sub">`. This grammar's query
captures keys as `@property`, so the style block below sets
`.hl-property` in bold; the colors come from the default palette.

```{=html}
<style>
.hl-property { font-weight: 600; }
</style>
```
